quests.name: Rats in the Walls
quests.description: Mira's provisions' cellar is crawling with giant rats, and the infestation runs deeper than any cellar should — down into a cave system nobody knew was there.

steps.name: Clear the cave under the shop
steps.description: Put down the giant rats swarming the cave beneath Mira's provisions.

steps.name: Clear out the basement nests
steps.description: The basement nests feed the cave below. Destroy them or the cellar refills within a season.

steps.name: Hunt down the strays around Hollowmere
steps.description: Giant rats are running all over town — please kill those buggers! Do this and prove your worth, and I'll gift you this Iron Key, which you'll surely need soon.

steps.name: Evict the goblin squatters
steps.description: Goblins have been slipping into one of Hollowmere's houses after dark — and where goblins nest, rats follow. Drive them out.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Twelve years I've kept this the legacy of Mira's shop and I have never once been beaten on a price — but I am being beaten by rats. Big ones, coming up through the basement faster than I can trap them, and I'd stake my black book it started with those goblins sneaking around after dark. Clear them out, top to bottom, and Mira Hask pays her debts.
quest_giver.end_dialog: A whole cave system. Under my shop. Twelve years standing on top of that, and not one supplier thought to mention it. The cellar's mine again, and your name goes in my book — the good column, which I'll have you know is the shorter one.

quests.name: The Grotto Below
quests.description: The rat infestation traces back to a goblin grotto north of town — and the goblins have been tunneling toward Hollowmere. Break the warren before the town wakes up with a basement it didn't dig.

steps.name: Clear the squatters from the upper grotto
Recover what the goblins stole
steps.description: The goblins took something from the town vault — the mayor is oddly vague about what. Find it in the lower grotto and bring it back unopened.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Goblins. In the grotto. Tunneling toward MY town, under MY shop district, on MY year as mayor. The Hask woman's rats were the warning and nobody listened, well, I'M listening, and I'm hiring. Break the warren, get back what they took from the vault, and try not to read anything you find down there. Town business stays town business.
quest_giver.end_dialog: You came back. Walking, even. I'll be honest, the town pool had you floating past the mill by Thursday — I lost three silver on you, and I have never been happier to lose money. The item goes back in the vault, the goblins go in the town record as 'resolved,' and you go on the list of people Hollowmere owes. It's a short list. We pay it.

quests.name: The Second Hole
quests.description: There's another grotto north of the goblin warren, and nobody in Hollowmere can say what's in it — which, lately, is reason enough to find out.

steps.name: Sound the grotto, top to bottom
steps.description: Walk every level of the second grotto and find out whether the holes connect.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Forty years of soldiering teaches you one thing worth keeping: it's never the hole you know about. There's a second grotto north of the goblin warren, and every soul in town walks past it like it isn't there. Go down it. All the way down. I'd go myself, but my knees signed a separate peace years ago.
quest_giver.end_dialog: So it's deep, and it's ugly, and now we know — which puts Hollowmere ahead of every town that found out the other way. You've done old Harl a kindness and the town a service. The town doesn't know it yet. They never do until the hole's full of something.

quests.name: Into the Dark Wood
quests.description: The old forest north of Hollowmere goes in further than it goes across, and the deeper paths stop being forest at all. Nobody has walked it end to end and said so afterward.

steps.name: Walk the Dark Wood to its end
steps.description: Map the dark woods at the top of the mountain range north of Hallowmere — through the deep boughs, the strangle-green, and whatever the paths become after that.

quest_giver.start_dialog: I came down from the fire mountains chasing a story: a wood to the south above that mountain range near Hallowmere that goes in further than it goes across, with old treasure where the paths stop behaving. My clan's singers say never walk a wrong wood alone, and I am — observe — alone. Walk it with me to the end. Whatever we find, we split. Whatever finds us, we share that too.
quest_giver.end_dialog: A winter clearing at the bottom of a summer wood. The singers will call me a liar, and I'll be rich enough not to care. You've earned your half — and a verse in the song, if I survive the singing of it.

quests.name: Pirates in Hollowmere
quests.description: Pirates — actual pirates, this far from any honest sea — have been raiding Hollowmere, and the trail runs through the town's least savory inn.

steps.name: Rescue the tavern-goers
steps.description: The pirates have loosed some nasty spiders in the inn. Chase those buggers out first, and I'll hand you some items that will surely help you finish the pirates off.

steps.name: Stop the raiders in the streets
Burn out the hideout under the inn

quest_giver.start_dialog: Pirates! In Hollowmere! We are NOWHERE NEAR THE SEA, friend, I checked — twice — and yet my entire troupe was robbed at cutlass-point not thirty paces from that lake. A jester knows misdirection when he's mugged by it: nobody sails to a lake. They're coming from somewhere, and my coin — what's left of it — says it's that unsavory inn.
quest_giver.end_dialog: My hero! My champion! My single remaining solvent acquaintance! The troupe returns tomorrow and the show goes on — juggling, tumbling, and a brand-new comic ballad entitled 'The Day the Pirates Picked the Wrong Lake.' You feature heavily. I'd pay you, but the town owes you and I AM the town's entertainment, so in a sense, you're already collecting. Bye bye!

quests.name: Wolves on the Tradeway
quests.description: The packs squatting on the road south of Varnfell aren't hunting deer — they're holding the road. Break them so the sledges can run again.

steps.name: Drive the wolf packs off the tradeway
steps.description: Hunt down the wolf packs lairing in the snowfields around Varnfell.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Twenty years trapping this country and I've never seen wolves hold a road like soldiers. Two packs, dug in on the tradeway, and every sledge in Varnfell stuck behind them. Clear them out and Sela can move her ledgers from red ink back to black.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Both packs broken — and you walked back out, which is better than the last three who tried. The tradeway's open. First sledge south carries word that Varnfell's still in business, and that's your doing.

quests.name: The Drowned Cargo
quests.description: A trade-sealed crate has washed up on the sand south of Varnfell. Sela Varn wants it back before the sea — or whatever paces the shore at night — takes it first.

steps.name: Recover the crate from the southern shore
steps.description: Find the trade-sealed crate Maro spotted on the sand south of town and bring it back. Something has been pacing that stretch of shore at night.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Maro logged a crate on the south sand — trade-sealed, which means it was bound for this post, which means it's mine. I'd send someone, but everyone I'd send is either behind this counter or buried. Bring it back whole and Varn and Daughters will remember you in the ledger, the good column.
quest_giver.end_dialog: The seal's my grandmother's mark — this crate left here forty years ago and the sea's only now giving it back. I don't know whether to thank you or apologize to you. Take this and we'll call it both.

quests.name: Into the Frost Delve
quests.description: The abandoned digging south of Varnfell has started breathing warm air. Henna Stone wants to know what's moved in below before it decides to move up.

steps.name: Explore the Frost Delve
steps.description: Descend the old workings and find the source of the warm air.

quest_giver.start_dialog: That delve was dead cold for nine years while I worked it, and dead quiet for twenty after. Now it breathes warm and the snow won't settle on the ridge. Go down, both levels, all the way to the warm dark — and come back and tell an old miner what's woken up under her town.
quest_giver.end_dialog: So the cracks do keep going down. I knew it — knew it when the company packed up, knew it every warm night since. You've bought Varnfell something nobody's had up here in a long while: warning. The town owes you, and so do I.

quests.name: The Royal Armory & The Ancient Dragon
quests.description: House Wellerman's relics were hidden from the dragon in a makeshift armory inside the Water Shrine, on an island far to the west. The cache has been found and seized. Take it back, arm your band, and put the Great Worm down for good.

steps.name: Destroy the Wyverns sent to block the royal armory
steps.description: The Water Shrine sits on an island far to the west; you'll need a boat, and rumor puts one hidden in Hollowmere. The dragon has loosed smaller wyrm-kin to guard the way — cut through them to reach the shrine.

steps.name: Clear out any remaining dragon born
steps.description: More wyverns lair in the depths of the Water Shrine. Destroy them.

steps.name: Retrieve the Royal Scrolls and Relics
steps.description: Inside the armory, recover House Wellerman's charter and arm yourselves with whatever relics you need to face the Great Worm.

steps.name: Descend into the Dragon's Cave and Destroy the Worm
steps.description: Descend into the cave on the island east of the capital and destroy the Ancient Dragon that has been tormenting the countryside.

quest_giver.start_dialog: My family's strongest weapons lie hidden from the dragon in a makeshift armory — the Water Shrine, on an island far to the west. The hiding place has been found and taken. You'll want those relics before the trials ahead: go east, secure the armory, arm your band, and then end the Great Worm.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Well fought. Now go forth and put the dragon down — before we turn to the harder task of driving the infernal horde back into its crack.

quests.name: The Withering
quests.description: Web spun wrong in the warden-trees and blight-root black in the sweetest soil of the Reach — the Heartwood Grove is sick with its keeper's worry, and Tansy Mosswane wants surgical help.

steps.name: Cut the web-blight out of the warden-trees
steps.description: Spinners are webbing the grove's warden-trees in patterns too regular to be honest spiderwork. Cut them out.

steps.name: Dig out the blight-root
steps.description: Find the blight-root under the grove's soured soil and bring it to Tansy whole — cut, not torn, so the grove heals clean.

quest_giver.start_dialog: The grove is sick the way a healer's house gets sick — from the keeper's own worry. Web in the warden-trees spun too regular, blight-root black where the soil was sweetest. Cut the spinners out and dig me that root whole. Iron's permitted in the ring for this; the treaty calls it surgery, and so do I.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Cut, not torn — you listened, which puts you ahead of every strong-armed helper I've ever hired. The root goes in the fire OUTSIDE the ring, the trees breathe easier already, and you'll take this salve kit because arguing with a Mosswane about payment has never once worked.

quests.name: The Sleepless Bough
quests.description: The Bough-Wife has not slept in four hundred nights, and the grove frays with her. Elder Bryn would settle her the old way: spring-water offered, the barrow quieted, and the haunted trail south swept clean.

steps.name: Draw water from the treaty-spring
steps.description: Draw the offering-water from the treaty-spring at dawn, the way the rite prescribes.

steps.name: Quiet the barrow
steps.description: The old barrow at the grove's edge has been muttering since the counting passed below. Put what rose back down.

steps.name: Sweep the haunted trail
steps.description: Something walks the forest road south of town at dusk, wearing the trail's old grief. The lady can't rest while it paces her fence-line.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Four hundred nights the lady's been awake, and a grove frays with its keeper. The old rite asks three things: water from her own spring, offered back — quiet in the barrow her roots wrap — and the trail south swept of whatever's pacing her fence-line at dusk. I can do the first. My knees and my sixty years cannot do the rest. Keep the rite's order, and strike no flame inside the ring.
quest_giver.end_dialog: She slept. Two hours, just past dawn — first time in four hundred nights, and the whole grove went still with her, every leaf, like a held breath finally let go. She woke calmer. She asked your names. Travelers — old things asking names is no small thing. Carry hers kindly, and take the circle's thanks in better coin.

quests.name: When the Forest Walks
quests.description: Nine felled warden-trees bought the Reach an angry forest: packs sitting the trails like sentries, a den fouling the sister-spring, and a troll moving under the boughs with a wolf escort. Warden Thornholt wants it ended before the moot has to learn the word 'siege.'

steps.name: Drive off the sentry packs
steps.description: Break the packs holding the forest road — the ones that sit, and watch, and do not eat.

steps.name: Break the den at the sister-spring
steps.description: Clear the den fouling the sister-spring south of town. The grove shares roots with that water.

steps.name: Put down the walker under the boughs
steps.description: End the troll that moves with a wolf escort before whatever gave it rank gives it orders.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Skell's nine trees lit a fuse, and what's burning down it isn't natural anger — packs posted like sentries, a den fouling the sister-spring, and a troll walking escorted under the boughs. Escorted. Something is organizing the forest's grudge, and Elderbough sits in the middle of it. Three jobs, south to north, and I'll walk every trail with you: packs, den, troll. In that order, or the survivors of each regroup with the next.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Packs broken, den cleared, and the troll down — I checked the track-lines this morning and the forest's moving like a forest again: feeding, hiding, minding its own seasons. The lady says the grudge is spent, and Skell wept at the tree-ring when Bryn told him, which I wasn't supposed to see and am telling everyone. The moot votes you its thanks. I just say it plainer: you gave me back a forest I can read.

quests.name: Lamps Against the Dark
quests.description: The dead are pressing Lastlight's wall by night and the watch is stretched past its last reserve. Captain Morn wants the warband broken, the bone-archers cleared from the crack-field, and the lost oil cache recovered before the lamps start choosing which streets go dark.

steps.name: Break the warband on the forest road
steps.description: A warband of the risen dead is circling toward the south gate through the trees. Break it before it finds the wall.

steps.name: Clear the bone-archers from the crack-field
steps.description: Skeleton archers have dug in among the rubble of the Near Crack, picking at the watch's warding-line crews.

steps.name: Recover the watch's oil cache
steps.description: The last supply run dropped the oil cache when the archers hit them. Lastlight's lamps are three nights from rationing — bring it home.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Here's the shape of my week: a warband of the walking dead circling my south road, bone-archers squatting in the crack-field shooting at my stone crews, and the oil cache for half the town's lamps lying out there where the supply run dropped it. The watch can hold the wall or fix all that — not both. You're the 'all that.' Warband first, archers second, oil last, and bring my people's arrows back out of yourselves if you can manage it.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Warband broken, field cleared, and the oil's already up the ladders — Tobb cried, which he'll deny. I've commanded this wall three years and tonight is the first night I've watched every lamp in Lastlight burning at full wick with nothing moving outside the ring. The watch pays its debts, and the watch says you're owed. That's not sentiment. It's arithmetic, and mine finally adds up.

quests.name: The Things in the Smoke
quests.description: Imps are slipping out of the Near Crack in threes — not raiding, surveying. Magister Corven needs them stopped mid-errand, both for the town's safety and for the chapter of his monograph he is increasingly afraid to finish.

steps.name: Intercept the skirmishers on the roads
steps.description: Pairs of imps have been ranging out from the crack along the forest roads, pausing at fords, lamp-posts, and waymarkers. Stop them mid-survey.

steps.name: Destroy the pack at the warding line
steps.description: A full pack has gathered at the watch's warding stones — looking, always looking. Make sure what it learned never gets back down the crack.

quest_giver.start_dialog: A research commission, plainly stated: the imps are surveying us — the wall, the lamps, the warding line — and everything they see walks back down that crack to whatever keeps their ledger. I require interrupted specimens. Stop the road-pairs mid-errand, destroy the pack at the warding stones, and observe as you work: what were they LOOKING at? Your sword settles the town's problem. Your eyes settle my chapter.
quest_giver.end_dialog: The warding stones — they were at the stones, of course, the locks of the line itself... and you say the road-pairs were studying the lamp-posts. The spacing. They were measuring the DARK between the lamps. Forgive me, I need to write this before my hands remember to shake. Your fee is on the table, doubled. The monograph will say the town was saved by capable field assistants, which is the highest compliment my discipline knows how to print.

quests.name: The Vigil Unbroken
quests.description: Something below has opened the graves of the first watch and seated a court among them — a lich, a banshee, and a thing in burial wrappings, holding session at the foot of the warding line while a herald of the breach stands attendance. Mother Halvane means the Vigil to hold, and the Vigil needs swords tonight.

steps.name: Disperse the Grave Court
steps.description: Break the court holding session among the graves of the first watch — the lich reads from a ledger that is not Mother Halvane's.

steps.name: Cast down the Herald of the Breach
steps.description: The hulking herald stands attendance at the crack's mouth with its imp retinue. End the session permanently.

steps.name: Recover the Warden's key
steps.description: The first watch's commander carried a key of black stone, lost when the watch fell. The court was holding session over the spot where it lies. Bring it to the chapel — not the captain, the chapel.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Listen to me, and weigh it before you accept, because I will not pretend this is wolf-work. The graves of the first watch stand open and a court sits among them — a lich with a ledger, a wailing thing, a horror in wrappings — and at the crack's mouth a herald attends them. They are holding session over my dead, reading names out of a book that is not mine. Break the court. Cast down the herald. And bring me the black key the first Warden carried, because I have begun to suspect what it fits, and I would rather be wrong in private.
quest_giver.end_dialog: The court is dispersed, the herald is down, and the names in the watch-yard answered tonight's reading like children answering roll — all of them, settled, for the first time since spring. As for the key... it is exactly what I feared, and exactly why I asked for swords I could trust. The first Warden didn't carry a key to the crack, traveler. He carried a key FROM it. Given, not taken. Which means once, long ago, what is below wanted this door kept — and the Vigil and I must now sit with what has changed its mind. Go and rest. You have bought the town time, and bought me the truth, and only one of those came cheap.

quests.name: The Horde Approaches
quests.description: Devils and demons are pouring out of the great crack and driving on the city, herding the imps ahead of them like a tide.

steps.name: Imp Army
steps.description: The devils are driving the imps toward the city walls. Break the charge.

quest_giver.start_dialog: All manner of devils and demons are rushing the city from the great crack — and they're driving the imps ahead of them like a tide! Hold the line with us!
quest_giver.end_dialog: Thank you, brave adventurers. But the work isn't done — the crack itself still breathes. Until we face the underworld at its source, there will be no peace.

quests.name: Find the Lost Citadel
quests.description: Somewhere beyond the crack stands a hidden fortress and the warriors who hold it — so secret that even the crown has lost its location. Find it.

steps.name: Find a way through The Crack
steps.description: Find a way to the far side of the crack — the path must lie hidden in one of the many dungeons in the mountains.

quest_giver.start_dialog: We hold a fortress on the far side of the crack — so secret that even we no longer know where it stands. Find a way across, find the citadel, and stand with the brave warriors holding the line there.
quest_giver.end_dialog: You found it, and they still stand. Word of the citadel changes everything — the war below the world has a foothold now, and a name.

quests.name: The Pale Court
quests.description: Sir Roderic Vane has hunted the vampire he calls the Pale Lord across thirty years and three duchies, and the trail has finally gone to ground close by in the Umbral Spire. Roderic's hands shake now. Yours don't.

steps.name: Destroy the Pale Lord's court
steps.description: In the Umbral Spire, the lord keeps a court of lesser vampires between himself and the door. Go through them.

steps.name: End the Pale Lord
steps.description: Face the Pale Lord himself. Roderic's advice: don't listen when it talks, and it will talk.

quest_giver.start_dialog: Thirty years. Three duchies. Every grave it left behind, I dug the proper way afterward, and I am very tired. It's gone to ground near here in the Umbral Spire — courted, fed, comfortable. I trained my whole life for the door at the bottom of that darkness, and now my hands won't hold the blade steady past sundown. So the hunt passes to you, as these things do. Take my notes. Take the sword's blessing. And when it talks — it will talk — you put it down mid-sentence.
quest_giver.end_dialog: Mid-sentence. Good. Thirty years, and it ends with me sitting by a fire hearing it secondhand — I expected that to hurt, and instead there's only the quiet. The notes are ash now, I burned them this morning; nobody needs to learn what I had to. The sword goes with you. It was never mine, you understand. It belongs to whoever finishes the hunt, and that was always going to be the part I wasn't there for.

quests.name: The Wailing Manor
quests.description: Corvin Ashe inherited the Wailing  Manor, which nobody has entered in sixty years, along with the wailing that comes off it at night. Somewhere inside is the family reliquary — and whatever has been keeping it.

steps.name: Breach the cursed halls
steps.description: The Wailing Manor's halls defend themselves. Fight through whatever the curse has made of the household.

steps.name: Silence the choir
steps.description: The wailing is a choir of banshees in the great hall. Silence it, or it will be the last sound you hear clearly.

steps.name: Destroy the master of the house
steps.description: Something old holds the deepest room and conducts the choir. End it.

steps.name: Recover the Ashe reliquary
steps.description: Find the family reliquary and bring it out into the daylight for the first time in sixty years.

quest_giver.start_dialog: I inherited a title, a The Wailing Manor, and a sound. The title is worthless, the manor is sealed, and the sound starts at dusk and stops when it notices you listening. The family reliquary is still inside — sixty years of Ashes too afraid to fetch it, and I'd like to be the generation that ends differently. I'll be honest, because my family never was: people who go in do not, as a rule, come out. Your rule may differ. The reliquary and my gratitude say it does.
quest_giver.end_dialog: The wailing stopped. Do you understand what that means to someone who grew up tuning it out? Sixty years of my family's shame, carried out in a box you could lift with two hands. I opened it. I won't tell you what's inside — some things should stay family — but I will tell you the Ashes pay their debts from this generation on, starting with the largest one we've ever owed.

quests.name: Seal the Crack
quests.description: Go into the great crack of the world and seal it shut

steps.name: Find the remaining Royal armory items
steps.description: Rumor holds that orcs stole the royal weapons and hid them in the Fire Shrine to the east. Take them back.

steps.name: Destroy the hydra
steps.description: A hydra has been summoned and bound to protect the royal stash. Destroy it before it destroys you.

steps.name: End the Pit Fiend
steps.description: Past the locked cavern, at the crack's mouth waits the Pit Fiend that commands the breach. Cast it down and seal the world shut behind it.

quest_giver.start_dialog: The time has come to finish this: descend into the great crack of the world and seal it shut. The road is long, and you will need every weapon and every ally you can gather along the way.
quest_giver.end_dialog: It is done. The crack is sealed, the warm dark below it gone quiet, and for the first time since spring the ground keeps its own counsel. The realm won't remember your names correctly — they never do — but it will go on. That was the whole of the work.

quests.name: The King's Message
quests.description: King Wellerman has declared that you must grow strong, and when you are ready you must see him for a quest to save the world from a foul dragon and an even worse threat from below the ground.

steps.name: Seek out Hallowmere
steps.description: Seak out the citizens of Hallowmere, they need your help and you must grow strong before seeing your King in the Capital to the East.

quest_giver.start_dialog: King Wellerman has declared that you must grow strong, and when you are ready you must see him for a quest to save the world from a foul dragon and an even worse threat from below the ground. Start by visiting Hallowmere to your South. The citizens there need your help and there you can start to grow strong. Once you are ready, seek out King Wellerman in the Capital toward the East.
